history.notes: Initial release candidate: one Philips Hue button accessory — dimmer switch, smart button, wall switch module, or tap dial including its rotary ring — relayed into Control4 programming over the bridge's local CLIP API v2 (HTTPS, developers.meethue.com). Clean-room original engineering, transport ported from the shipped IntegrateIT Hue Bridge driver. · Link-button pairing built in: Pair (Link Button) POSTs `/api` with `generateclientkey`, handles the error-101 "press the button" round-trip, and stores the returned application key in the password-typed property — never printed, never logged (it rides only in the `hue-application-key` header). · Accessory binding: List Accessories enumerates every bridge device that owns a `button` service and prints its name, device id, button count, and whether it has a dial. Paste the id into **Accessory Device ID** (a button / rotary / power service id of the same accessory resolves to its owner) and the binding persists across a reboot; changing it clears battery, identity, and every `LAST_*` event detail back to unknown (the bridge reachability baseline is deliberately kept — the bridge did not change, and dropping it would swallow the next genuine Went Offline). · Per-button events for the documented CLIP v2 `button_report.event` vocabulary — `initial_press`, `repeat`, `short_release`, `long_release`, `double_short_release` — on `metadata.control_id` 1-4, plus a catch-all **Button Event** that fires for every button report and carries `LAST_BUTTON` / `LAST_EVENT`. An event value outside the five named ones (the enum also carries `long_press` in third-party mirrors of the login-gated Signify reference) reaches Composer through the catch-all with the literal string in `LAST_EVENT` — never renamed into something this build cannot account for, never dropped. · Tap dial ring: **Rotary Clockwise** / **Rotary Counterclockwise** from `relative_rotary.rotary_report.rotation`, with `LAST_ROTARY_DIRECTION` and `LAST_ROTARY_STEPS` carrying the raw `direction` and `steps`. An unrecognized direction is logged, not guessed at. · Battery from `device_power`: `BATTERY_LEVEL` and `BATTERY_STATE` mirrors plus a **Battery Low** event derived from the official `battery_state` enum (`normal` / `low` / `critical`) on a change from an already-known state — no invented percentage threshold. · THE EVENT CONTRACT, enforced in code and stated plainly in the docs: a button press is transient and exists only on `/eventstream/clip/v2`. The driver sends no `Last-Event-ID`, so it requests no replay; and the REST read path — which is handed each button's stored `button_report` on every enumeration — has **no code path to `C4:FireEvent` for a button at all**. A press made while the stream is down is lost permanently, and nothing here will fabricate one from a stored report that cannot say when it happened. Programming built on presses must tolerate that loss. `BRIDGE_ONLINE`, **Went Online** / **Went Offline**, and **Event Stream Reconnected** exist so a project can see the blind window; a stream close alone never declares the bridge offline (that verdict belongs to a REST read that gets no answer). · Baseline silence throughout: the first reachability observation, the first battery reading, and every replayed or stored button/rotary report are adopted without firing anything. Only a real change from an already-known value fires. · Events-only by construction: the package declares **no Control4 proxy** and ships `combo: true` — there is no Navigator surface, because this driver cannot drive the switch it listens to. Pair it with IntegrateIT Hue Bridge to control lights, groups, and scenes. · LAN guard at the transport chokepoint (`HueRequest` and `OpenEventStream` both re-run it), so no caller — including the boot-time enumeration, the refresh heartbeat, pairing, and Test Connection — can put the application key on a packet bound off-LAN. Refusals are local, named, and carry the reason. · Frame discipline, because a dropped frame is a dropped press: the CLIP JSON scanner is string-aware, so brackets and braces inside a customer-typed Hue name (`Sconce ]`, `Nook {1`) are text and cannot truncate a payload, hide the resources behind them, or merge two objects into one; SSE framing accepts `CRLF` as well as `LF`; and exactly one eventstream is ever believed at a time — Reconnect Event Stream and any bridge-identity change retire the current one by generation, so a superseded socket can neither double-deliver a press nor keep repainting `BRIDGE_ONLINE` from an address the LAN guard has started refusing. · Honest TLS trust model: the bridge is self-signed, so the driver connects over HTTPS with CA verification disabled and pins trust to the LAN address + application key; a broken TLS handshake fails closed and never downgrades to plaintext. Bounded eventstream reconnect (5s → 60s cap) and MAC-locked IntegrateIT licensing on every event delivery. · Hue Developer Terms: this is an automation trigger source, explicitly **not** for security or surveillance use. · Known limits: one accessory per instance; named events cover `control_id` 1-4; no motion/contact sensors, no lights/groups/scenes, no entertainment API; on an OS build without `C4:url` streaming there is no eventstream and therefore no events at all (the driver says so in Device Status rather than pretending to listen).
